title: Quick check: Proxy Use Cases

questions.prompt: In the context of “Proxy Use Cases” and “Header modification”, In Next.js 16, which name replaces the deprecated Middleware convention in current documentation?
questions.explanation: The version-specific documentation renames Middleware to Proxy; older applications still need legacy maintenance guidance.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Proxy Use Cases”, What is an appropriate use of Proxy?
options: A universal substitute for authorization inside every protected server action.
A persistent worker for long-running background jobs in every host.
Selective request-time routing or lightweight request handling where supported by the deployment model.
A place to store secrets in browser code.
questions.answer_key: Selective request-time routing or lightweight request handling where supported by the deployment model.
questions.explanation: Proxy can shape some incoming requests but does not replace permission checks in the final protected operation.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Proxy Use Cases”, What should guide the use of framework configuration options?
options: Check the version-matched official reference and verify the setting in development and production builds.
Assume every option works across all releases and hosts.
Copy experimental settings without documenting them.
Disable tests to avoid configuration errors.
questions.answer_key: Check the version-matched official reference and verify the setting in development and production builds.
questions.explanation: Framework configuration and platform support are version- and host-dependent.
